items.title: Over a Jacobson base the finite type points have transcendence degree zero

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: if f : X -> Y is locally of finite type over a scheme S, Y is Jacobson and x is a finite type point of X, then the transcendence degree of x over f(x) is 0 (source lines 6811-6819). The proof chooses surjective etale presentations V -> Y and U -> X x_Y V, lifts x to a finite type point u of U using the surjectivity of the finite type points, shrinks U so that u is closed, and then applies the scheme statement over the Jacobson base V to conclude that kappa(u) is finite over kappa(v), which is the assertion about the transcendence degree.
